The factor of the input voltage is also considered and it was determined that the range of the sensor’s output voltage varies with input voltages. Each transducer has different input voltage providing maximum output voltage. Moreover, the transducer’s dimension has an affect on the sensor’s sensitivity. The transducer that has 0.65-in wide gives the highest sensitivity on both 0.030-in and 0.065-in Al. In addition, sheet metal type also has an effect on the sensitivity of the transducers because all transducers work well with aluminum but less sensitive with steel. Thus, the sensor is sensitive to the amount of irons in the material (aluminum is non-ferrous but steel is ferrous). In order to obtain a better result from testing steel, the input voltage has to be reduced to a certain value. The graphical comparisons of each transducer while testing with different materials can be found in Appendix B.

IIn the actual stamping process, sheet metal can become wrinkled when it is stamped. Thus, experimenting with wrinkled sheet metal will determine the effectiveness of the draw-in sensor. However, using only a single-transducer prototype will not yield a linear result because the shape of wrinkled sheet metal creates inconsistent gaps between the transducer and the sheet metal. The solution to this problem is to create double-transducer prototype that places one transducer on top and the other under a wrinkled sheet metal. Consequently, the sum of the readings from each transducer will generate linear results.
